title: 3M P2 Respirator 9123 Disposable Face Mask (Carton of 400 Masks) $129 Delivered @ South East Clearance
body:
Deal: 3M P2 Respirator 9123 Disposable Face Mask (Carton of 400 Masks) $129 Delivered @ South East Clearance

[huntingforbargainz] In that case the masks should be placed in the museum at this point.
[adamreid] Yeah (profanity) immunocompromised people right?
[adamreid] "MASK discount code isn’t valid for the items in your cart"
[DIYcharcat] its working now, have refunded the shipping on anyone whose purchased
[xmagic] Have to say I hated these earloop 3M P2 masks back in COVID. Headband models are way more comfortable.
[Goonos] These can be worn either way, they come with clips to attach as a headband (just stretch out the elastic loops)
[xmagic] Yes, but that clip is just a band-aid. The clip will make the mask super tight, given the ear loops themselves are already quite tight to ensure a seal.
[adamreid] I've been wearing this model since 2021, and haven't had covid. It's an extremely good mask if you use the clip. The clip doesn't place any strain on your ear cartilage The tight seal is a good thing imo.
[Goonos] The elastic has lots of give so you just stretch it out. It will then permantly loose some elasticity so its not tight (though can't then place them around the ears anymore as they have been stretch too far)
[outlander] You sure that wasn't the Bunnings model?
I bought this type and the bunnings type when they were clearing them out at $1 per 5pk. The 3m ones were okay: you might feel the tightness if your wearing them for hours. Whereas the bunnings ones were made for child sized heads and started pinching immediately.
[xmagic] @outlander: No, it was the standard models. Short job, yeah, likely won’t be an issue. This mask is definitely not for an extended session.
[dufflover] But looking at the shop picture it still presses down on the top of the ears which is the most uncomfortable part, for me at least.
I don't mind ear loops for the odd quick DIY job but anything longer would go with a headband. Too many to stock up on here lol
[gakko] Yep good call saved me from an impulse purchase. Good deal nonetheless
[chumpychops] Have gone through several hundred of these for work in a dust application over the last two years
They are indeed a good fit on the face for myself and colleagues. The earloops suit our brief applications on again/ off again.
A head loop is way more comfortable for extended use and The clip does tighten the straps too much for my liking making them less effective for this.
stretching the elastic to make them looser didn’t work for me, because the airloop would just break before the right stretch point t was found.
Still a good mask - in our specific usage case
[Ganbaru] Can you do free sihpping for 25 packs too
[Ultraman] 400/8=50 per month, not too hard to do if using em on site every day.
[adamreid] The actual masks don't stop working magically, the reason they have a 5 year shelf life is that's how long the elastics are rated for. Masks don't turn into a pumpkin at 5 years they'll still be fine for a long time. https://smartairfilters.com/en/blog/do-n95-masks-expire/
[King Tightarse] If the elastics break after a certain date that is a good reason to put a shelf life on them.
Just need them to work without issues when you need them
[THEMAN_AUS] Im tempted to order, because the filthy woman on the plane I was on wouldnt stop coughing and I got sick when I landed.
[ReaperX22] Unfortunately this won't help you that massively on planes. It can reduce chances but if you're near people like that, given the pressure and the low humidity inside planes in the air, airborne viruses are pretty hard to dodge on flights.. I ended up both with a month long cold/flu and gastro after a long flight from Syd to Paris, I lost 2 full days from the gastro (I stayed hotel, sent partner to roam and do some things we already had pre booked).. Then on off our entire euro trip (honeymoon couple years back) we were just constantly sick. Really sucked tbh. Partner didn't get the gastro thankfully, so that likely came from surfaces or a difference of food choice on one of our flights!
It certainly doesn't help that those who ARE sick already rarely do the courtesy of covering their mouths, using masks themselves, sanitising and just love touching all the surfaces lol.
Edit for anyone reading as well:
Long haul flights these masks are gonna be UNCOMFORTABLE AS HELL. You'll wait ones that are designed to be back of head rather than over ears (clip adapters are horrible imo), or more of a fancier re usable fabric style (AusAir, though I'm skeptical how well these work long term. They do have 50% off atm! I'm tempted to try..)
[Goonos] I noticed during COVID that I finally stopped picking up colds from planes because I was forced to wear a mask. So now for long haul flights I wear them and from my ancedontal experience seems to help. Also helps if people have bad B.O around you.
[eug] Unfortunately this won't help you that massively on planes. It can reduce chances but if you're near people like that, given the pressure and the low humidity inside planes in the air, airborne viruses are pretty hard to dodge on flights.
How does low pressure and low humidity affect how well an N95 mask works?
[ReaperX22] It's less about the mask, and more about the environment.. This is more for long-haul flights, eventually you have to eat, go bathroom, etc. You'll breath air in at some point without a mask… I've not really known anyone recently who's taken a flight and not gotten sick
[ihbh] If you need these for work, note that 3M half mask respirators can be had for < $50 on sale (e.g. Bunnings/Amazon); full mask respirators are a bit over $214 at Bunnings/Amazon at the moment.
For shopping, etc., I'll leave it up to you to decide.
[dhx] I have and would recommend https://www.totaltools.com.au/catalogue-offers/safety-equipm… (or similar) for DIY/tradies as a full face mask is much better protection and also much more comfortable. Fine to wear for hours without discomfort, fogging up, etc. Even though these type of P3 full face masks claim to be for asbestos or spray painting use, I think PAPR masks would be better suited for those risks. P2 masks I wouldn't trust for their claimed protection against silica dust, especially when P3 full face masks aren't much more expensive (won't need to buy eye protection either) and are far more comfortable to work with.
[h0mbre] These are good masks but not for my use case as I am a builder and these would be for my boys doing demolition etc
I'm tempted to buy them because of the price but I know my boys will whine about the ear loops and no valve.
I used to buy the Honeywell masks that regularly got posted on here pre-covid. I prob bought 1000s. Haven't a good deal for quality masks like that since.
